headline: Pawtucket High School construction contract, $274,459,564 with Shawmut Design and Construction, approved.
summary: The price covers construction of a 367,000-square-foot career and technical high school. The schedule now calls for substantial completion on November 1, 2028, and final completion on February 28, 2029, two months earlier than before. Members also approved a $240,229 owner's project manager contract with Colliers Project Leaders. They approved a $245,000 master planning contract with Civic.
decisions: Approved a girls' flag football program for a Pawtucket unified team, 6-0.
Approved an updated district organizational chart, 6-0, with the superintendent to add names and salary ranges.
Approved a $245,000 master planning contract with Civic, 4-2.
Approved a $240,229 owner's project manager contract with Colliers Project Leaders, 6-0.
Approved a guaranteed maximum price contract of $274,459,564 with Shawmut Design and Construction for Pawtucket High School, 6-0.
Approved the Cunningham Elementary School playground fencing and gate installation, 6-0.
Approved a $148,900 contract with Delta Mechanical Contractors to replace the hot water tank at Jenks Middle School, 6-0.
Approved a $16,420 contract with Oak Hill Farm, LLC for pre-K playground fencing at Nathaniel Greene Elementary School, funded by a state grant, 6-0.
Approved a $39,000 contract with Fiore Roofing & Construction for upper roof gutter repairs at Nathaniel Greene Elementary School, funded by a state grant, 6-0.
discussion: Teacher contract approval: Public speakers asked the committee to urge the city council to approve the 3-year contract, saying teachers have waited since August 25th. Members said they had asked for updates on the council's review.

Master planning and redistricting: Members asked why redistricting is being done again after last year's effort. The administration said the work will update demographics, test boundary scenarios, and support the Stage II application due February 15, 2027.

OPM bid comparison: The two bids were Colliers Project Leaders at $240,229 and LeftField at $135,377. Some members raised concerns about LeftField's knowledge of the district, and the administration said Colliers' experience with district projects and the deadline were key.

Food service safety response: Members asked why a food safety incident took four days before families were told. Aramark said the response should have been faster and described changes to its process, and members asked for a written plan with a timeline.
Parking at new high school: Members asked whether there is enough parking. A student parking survey is being reviewed, and the meeting gave a count of 308 parking spots on site.
